LESSON: ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSIONS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Algebra
Topic 2.1: Algebraic Expressions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Algebraic Expressions. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we use algebraic expressions in daily activities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. form algebraic expressions from real-life situations
2. form algebraic expressions from simple algebraic statements in real-life situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Algebraic Expressions.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Algebraic Expressions using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss and classify objects in their immediate environment according to given attributes such as similarities or differences
2. Discuss how to form algebraic expressions from the classified objects
3. Read and interpret algebraic statements to form algebraic expressions
4. Discuss how to simplify algebraic expressions from the classified objects
5. Communication and Collaboration: speaking, listening, and teamwork as the learner discusses on the formation of algebraic expressions.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Algebraic Expressions is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
